title: Circuit Folding: Scalable and Graph-Based Circuit Cutting via Modular Structure Exploitation
problem: Circuit cutting for quantum circuit partitioning on NISQ hardware relies on graph-based methods that face prohibitively high computational complexity when identifying optimal cutting locations, especially under realistic hardware constraints.
motivation: Executing large quantum circuits on NISQ hardware requires effective circuit cutting that leverages both quantum and classical resources, but existing approaches struggle with scalability and computational efficiency.
method: CiFold introduces a graph-based framework exploiting repetitive modular structures in quantum algorithms. The approach systematically folds quantum circuits into compact meta-graphs by identifying and merging common gate sequences across entangled qubits. Folding factor and variance quantify circuit compression and ensure balanced folding. Using condensed representations, CiFold identifies cut locations without exhaustive global graph searches.
key_novelty: Exploitation of repetitive modular quantum circuit structures through circuit folding to enable scalable and efficient identification of optimal cutting locations.
contributions: Circuit folding technique identifying and merging common gate sequences for compact meta-graph representation
Folding factor and variance metrics quantifying circuit compression and balance
Scalable cut location identification without exhaustive global search
Average 31.6% reduction in required cuts and 3.55× 10⁹ reduction in sampling overhead

metrics.other: 31.6% reduction in cuts, 3.55×10⁹ sampling overhead reduction

limitations: Evaluation limited to quantum algorithm classes with regular modular structures; applicability to irregular or highly optimized quantum circuits is not discussed.
primary_theme: Scalable quantum circuit cutting via folding
